1: //! # Good Practices: Common best-practice checks for MATLAB code
2: //!
3: //! This module implements 59 good-practice checks from MATLAB's Code Analyzer,
4: //! handled by a single hybrid engine (`GoodPracticesEngine`). Node-level checks
5: //! cover simple pattern matches (error handling, eval usage, string comparisons,
6: //! parfor/spmd usage), while file-level checks use metadata extraction and the
7: //! symbol table for context-aware analysis.
8: //!
9: //! ## Check IDs
10: //!
11: //! ### Error handling
12: //!
13: //! | Check ID | Description |
14: //! |----------|-------------|
15: //! | TRYNC    | `try` without `catch` |
16: //! | CTCH     | `catch` block is empty |
17: //! | WLAST    | `warning` called as last statement in function |
18: //! | WNTAG    | `warning` without message ID |
19: //! | ERTAG    | `error` without message ID |
20: //! | MEXCEP   | `catch` without exception variable |
21: //!
22: //! ### String / comparison
23: //!
24: //! | Check ID | Description |
25: //! |----------|-------------|
26: //! | STCMP    | Use `strcmp`/`strcmpi` instead of `==` for strings |
27: //! | STCI     | Use `strcmpi` for case-insensitive comparison |
28: //! | STISA    | Use `isa` instead of `class` + `strcmp` |
29: //! | STRNU    | Use `str2double` instead of `str2num` |
30: //!
31: //! ### Eval / dynamic code
32: //!
33: //! | Check ID   | Description |
34: //! |------------|-------------|
35: //! | EVLCS      | Avoid `eval` |
36: //! | EVLDOT     | Avoid `eval` for dynamic field access |
37: //! | EVLEQ      | Avoid `eval` for dynamic variable creation |
38: //! | EVLSYS     | Avoid `eval` for system commands |
39: //! | EVLDUAL    | Avoid `evalin` |
40: //! | EVLSEQVAR  | Avoid `eval` to create sequential variables |
41: //!
42: //! ### General practices
43: //!
44: //! | Check ID    | Description |
45: //! |-------------|-------------|
46: //! | NOANS       | Statement result assigned to `ans` |
47: //! | LOAD        | `load` without output variable |
48: //! | SEPEX       | Multiple statements on one line |
49: //! | NBRAK1      | Unnecessary brackets around scalar |
50: //! | LNGNM       | Variable name exceeds length |
51: //! | CHAIN       | Method chaining on one line |
52: //! | DISPLAY     | Override `display` is discouraged |
53: //! | FNDEF       | Function not defined at expected location |
54: //! | NOIN        | Function has no input validation |
55: //! | VALST       | Validate function arguments |
56: //! | PROP        | Property validation missing |
57: //! | CPROP       | Constant property could be method |
58: //! | FVAL        | Function value not used |
59: //! | FNCOLND     | `end` used as column index without dimension |
60: //! | COMNC       | Comment lacks space after `%` |
61: //! | ITERS       | Loop variable shadows outer variable |
62: //! | LOGPROD     | Use `all` instead of `prod` on logical |
63: //! | LOGMIN      | Use `all` instead of `min` on logical |
64: //! | LOGMAX      | Use `any` instead of `max` on logical |
65: //! | ELARLOG     | Element-wise `&`/`|` on logicals in if/while |
66: //! | SHOCIRAA    | Short-circuit in array context |
67: //! | UNRPWR      | Power of negative base may be complex |
68: //! | ADAPPREF    | Avoid `addpref` (use settings) |
69: //! | KEYBOARDFUN | `keyboard` left in code |
70: //! | GVMIS       | Global variable used but never declared |
71: //!
72: //! ### Parfor / SPMD / parallel practices
73: //!
74: //! | Check ID | Description |
75: //! |----------|-------------|
76: //! | PFEVB     | Using EVALIN('base') or ASSIGNIN('base') inside a PARFOR loop refers to the worker machines' base workspaces |
77: //! | PFGP      | Avoid assigning to GLOBAL or PERSISTENT variable inside a PARFOR loop |
78: //! | PFGV      | Avoid using GLOBAL variable in a PARFOR loop |
79: //! | PFIIN     | The input variable should be initialized before the PARFOR loop |
80: //! | PFOUS     | The output variable might not be used after the PARFOR loop |
81: //! | PFRNI     | Do not specify the increment explicitly; parfor can only use an increment of one |
82: //! | PFRIN     | The reduction variable might not be set before the PARFOR loop |
83: //! | PFRUS     | The reduction variable might not be used after the PARFOR loop |
84: //! | PFTUSW    | The temporary variable might be used after the PARFOR loop |
85: //! | PFUIXW    | The index variable might be used after the PARFOR loop |
86: //! | SPEVB     | Using EVALIN('base') or ASSIGNIN('base') inside an SPMD block refers to the worker machines' base workspaces |
87: //! | SPGV      | Using the GLOBAL or PERSISTENT variable in an SPMD block might fail because it is accessed on a worker machine |
88: //! | DSPMDA    | Distributed array must be created outside of an SPMD block |
89: //!
90: //! ### Structure / string / misc
91: //!
92: //! | Check ID | Description |
93: //! |----------|-------------|
94: //! | COMFS     | Comma makes the file a script, so functions are local |
95: //! | DUALC     | Command might be prematurely ended by comma |
96: //! | RMFLD     | `rmfield` output must be assigned back to the structure |
97: //! | RMWRN     | Warning tag has been removed from MATLAB |
98: //! | SEMFS     | Semicolon makes the file a script, so functions are local |
99: //! | STFLD     | `setfield` output must be assigned back to the structure |
100: //! | STRSZ     | Use `strcmp` to compare character vectors of different sizes |
101: //!
102: //! ### OOP / class / property
103: //!
104: //! | Check ID | Description |
105: //! |----------|-------------|
106: //! | ATTF     | Unable to determine if the expression assigned to the `Abstract` attribute evaluates to true or false |
107: //! | ATTOF    | Setting the class attribute `Abstract` to false is not recommended |
108: //! | MCPO     | `SetObservable`/`GetObservable`/`AbortSet` property has no effect in a value class |
109: //! | MCSAC    | `SetAccess` cannot be set on Constant properties |
110: //! | MOBSRV   | `SetObservable`/`GetObservable` on a Constant property has no effect |
111: //! | MDEPIN   | Default values should not be assigned to dependent properties |
112: //! | MCCPI    | Initialize the Constant property or make it an Abstract Constant property |
113: //! | MGMD     | `get` method should be implemented for each dependent property without private `GetAccess` |
114: //! | MCCPE    | Attempting to call a property or event as a function |
115: //! | MTHANS   | Using `ANS` as a method name is not recommended |
116: //! | MHERM    | Parenthesize the multiplication of a variable and its transpose |
117: //! | MNUML    | Use `VAR_NAME(numel(...), numel(...))` to create a square matrix |
118: //!
119: //! ### Logical / comparison / range
120: //!
121: //! | Check ID | Description |
122: //! |----------|-------------|
123: //! | COMPNOP   | Comparison with `true` simplifies to the function call itself |
124: //! | COMPNOT   | Comparison with `~= true` or `== false` simplifies to `~call(...)` |
125: //! | M3COL     | Three colons (`a:b:c:d`) in an expression is probably unintended |
126: //!
127: //! ### Logical usage / handle defaults / shared variables / arity
128: //!
129: //! | Check ID | Description |
130: //! |----------|-------------|
131: //! | BDLGI    | Variable might be set by a nonlogical operator |
132: //! | BDLOG1   | Non-scalar logical value used in a conditional expression |
133: //! | BDLOG2   | Scalar non-logical value used in a conditional expression |
134: //! | BDSCA    | `&&`/`||` used in a scalar context with a non-scalar operand |
135: //! | BDSCI    | Variable might be set by a nonscalar operator |
136: //! | MCHDP    | Property default that directly constructs a handle is shared by all instances |
137: //! | MCHDT    | Property default that resolves to a handle is shared by all instances |
138: //! | SHVAU    | Ambiguous shared-variable usage between a nested function and its parent |
139: //! | GTARG    | Function might be called with too many arguments |
140: //! | LTARG    | Function might be called with too few arguments |
141: //!
142: //! ### Function-call conventions
143: //!
144: //! | Check ID | Description |
145: //! |----------|-------------|
146: //! | CTPCT    | `sprintf`/`fprintf` format might not agree with the argument count |
147: //! | FXSET    | Loop index variable is changed inside of a `for` loop |
148: //! | SIMPT    | `import` statement does not run first in a function |
149: //! | TLEV     | Dynamic-code function used as a sub-expression, not a top-level statement |
150: //! | UNONC    | `onCleanup` output must be assigned to a variable, not `~` |
151: //! | MIPC1    | `computer('arch')` is platform-specific |
152: //! | SUBSINDEX | Do not overload `subsindex` for fundamental data types |
153: //! | VTFIN    | Validated value should be the first input to a `validate*` function |
154: //! | CTOINW   | Constructed object passed to its own constructor |
155: //! | FXUP     | Outer loop index set inside a nested function |
156: //!
157: //! ### App Designer
158: //!
159: //! | Check ID | Description |
160: //! |----------|-------------|
161: //! | ADMTHDINV | Class method called without `app` as the first argument |
162: //! | ADPROP   | Property assigned through a bare identifier instead of `app.PROP` |
163: //! | ADPROPLC | Property read through a bare identifier instead of `app.PROP` |
164: //!
165: //! ### OOP practice
166: //!
167: //! | Check ID | Description |
168: //! |----------|-------------|
169: //! | MCNPN    | Member access on the object that is not declared in the class |
170: //! | MCNPR    | Assignment target on the object that is not a property |
171: //! | MCSNOV   | Value-class setter does not return the modified object |
172: //! | MCSOH    | Handle-class setter unnecessarily returns the modified object |
173: //! | MCVM     | Value-class method modifying the object has no output |
174: //! | MCCSPS   | Constant property name used as a struct in a dot-access chain |
175: //! | MCSUP    | Setter accesses a property other than the one it sets |

366:     /// WLAST: `warning` is the last statement in a function (may need `error` instead).
367:     fn check_wlast(&self, tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
368:         if !self.is_check_enabled("WLAST") {
369:             return Vec::new();
370:         }
371: 
372:         let meta = FileMeta::build(tree, source);
373:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
374: 
375:         for func in &meta.functions {
376:             self.check_wlast_in_range(
377:                 tree.root_node(),
378:                 source,
379:                 func.byte_range.clone(),
380:                 &mut diagnostics,
381:             );
382:         }
383:         for func in &meta.local_functions {
384:             self.check_wlast_in_range(
385:                 tree.root_node(),
386:                 source,
387:                 func.byte_range.clone(),
388:                 &mut diagnostics,
389:             );
390:         }
391: 
392:         diagnostics
393:     }

395:     /// Helper: check if the last statement in a byte range is a `warning()` call.
396:     fn check_wlast_in_range(
397:         &self,
398:         root: Node,
399:         source: &str,
400:         range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
401:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
402:     ) {
403:         // Find the function_definition node covering this range.
404:         let func_node = find_node_in_range(root, &range);
405:         let func_node = match func_node {
406:             Some(n) if n.kind() == "function_definition" => n,
407:             _ => return,
408:         };
409: 
410:         // Get the block child (function body).
411:         let block = match find_child_of_kind(func_node, "block") {
412:             Some(b) => b,
413:             None => return,
414:         };
415: 
416:         // Find the last named non-`end` child.
417:         let last_stmt = last_named_child_not_end(block);
418:         let last_stmt = match last_stmt {
419:             Some(s) => s,
420:             None => return,
421:         };
422: 
423:         // Check if it's a warning() call.
424:         if last_stmt.kind() != "function_call" {
425:             return;
426:         }
427:         let name = get_function_call_name(last_stmt, source);
428:         if name != Some("warning") {
429:             return;
430:         }
431: 
432:         let pos = last_stmt.start_position();
433:         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
434:             rule_id: "WLAST",
435:             message: "warning() is the last statement in this function; did you mean error()?"
436:                 .to_string(),
437:             severity: Severity::Warning,
438:             byte_range: last_stmt.start_byte()..last_stmt.end_byte(),
439:             line: pos.row + 1,
440:             column: pos.column + 1,
441:             fix: None,
442:         });
443:     }

445:     /// RMFLD: `rmfield` result must be assigned back to the structure.
446:     fn check_rmfld(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
447:         self.check_struct_assign_back(node, source, "rmfield", "RMFLD")
448:     }

450:     /// STFLD: `setfield` result must be assigned back to the structure.
451:     fn check_stfld(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
452:         self.check_struct_assign_back(node, source, "setfield", "STFLD")
453:     }

455:     /// Shared RMFLD/STFLD logic: fire when the call is a standalone statement
456:     /// (parent is `source_file`/`block`) so its result is silently discarded.
457:     fn check_struct_assign_back(
458:         &self,
459:         node: Node,
460:         source: &str,
461:         func_name: &str,
462:         check_id: &'static str,
463:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
464:         if !self.is_check_enabled(check_id) || node.kind() != "function_call" {
465:             return Vec::new();
466:         }
467:         if get_function_call_name(node, source) != Some(func_name) {
468:             return Vec::new();
469:         }
470:         if !is_statement_level(node) {
471:             return Vec::new();
472:         }
473: 
474:         let pos = node.start_position();
475:         vec![Diagnostic {
476:             rule_id: check_id,
477:             message: format!(
478:                 "{} output must be assigned back to the structure",
479:                 func_name.to_uppercase()
480:             ),
481:             severity: Severity::Warning,
482:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
483:             line: pos.row + 1,
484:             column: pos.column + 1,
485:             fix: None,
486:         }]
487:     }
488: 
489:     /// PFIIN / PFOUS / PFTUSW / PFUIXW: PARFOR loop data-flow checks.
490:     ///
491:     /// Uses the symbol table with byte-range comparisons because the symbol
492:     /// table has no per-parfor scope.
493:     fn check_parfor_file_level(&self, tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
494:         let any_enabled = self.is_check_enabled("PFIIN")
495:             || self.is_check_enabled("PFOUS")
496:             || self.is_check_enabled("PFTUSW")
497:             || self.is_check_enabled("PFUIXW");
498:         if !any_enabled {
499:             return Vec::new();
500:         }
501: 
502:         let sym = SymbolTable::build(tree, source);
503:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
504:         let parfors = collect_parfor_nodes(tree.root_node(), source);
505: 
506:         for parfor in &parfors {
507:             let idx_var = extract_parfor_index_var(*parfor, source);
508:             let body = find_child_of_kind(*parfor, "block");
509: 
510:             // PFIIN: input variable read in the body but never initialized
511:             // before the loop and not assigned inside the loop.
512:             if self.is_check_enabled("PFIIN") {
513:                 if let Some(body_node) = body {
514:                     let mut skip = std::collections::HashSet::new();
515:                     if let Some(ref idx) = idx_var {
516:                         skip.insert(idx.clone());
517:                     }
518:                     let reads = collect_parfor_body_reads(body_node, source, &skip);
519:                     for (name, read_node) in reads {
520:                         if is_defined_before_parfor(&sym, &name, parfor.start_byte())
521:                             || is_assigned_in_body(body_node, &name, source)
522:                         {
523:                             continue;
524:                         }
525:                         let pos = read_node.start_position();
526:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
527:                             rule_id: "PFIIN",
528:                             message: format!(
529:                                 "The input variable {name} should be initialized before the PARFOR loop."
530:                             ),
531:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
532:                             byte_range: read_node.start_byte()..read_node.end_byte(),
533:                             line: pos.row + 1,
534:                             column: pos.column + 1,
535:                             fix: None,
536:                         });
537:                     }
538:                 }
539:             }
540: 
541:             // PFOUS / PFTUSW: simple-identifier assignments in the body and
542:             // whether the variable is used after the loop.
543:             let need_assignments =
544:                 self.is_check_enabled("PFOUS") || self.is_check_enabled("PFTUSW");
545:             if need_assignments {
546:                 if let Some(body_node) = body {
547:                     let assigned = collect_simple_lhs_assignments(body_node, source);
548:                     for (name, lhs_node) in assigned {
549:                         if idx_var.as_deref() == Some(name.as_str()) {
550:                             continue;
551:                         }
552:                         let uses = uses_after_parfor(&sym, &name, parfor.end_byte(), tree, false);
553:                         if self.is_check_enabled("PFOUS") && uses.is_empty() {
554:                             let pos = lhs_node.start_position();
555:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
556:                                 rule_id: "PFOUS",
557:                                 message: format!(
558:                                     "The output variable {name} might not be used after the PARFOR loop."
559:                                 ),
560:                                 severity: Severity::Warning,
561:                                 byte_range: lhs_node.start_byte()..lhs_node.end_byte(),
562:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
563:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
564:                                 fix: None,
565:                             });
566:                         }
567:                         if self.is_check_enabled("PFTUSW") {
568:                             if let Some(line) = uses.first() {
569:                                 let pos = lhs_node.start_position();
570:                                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
571:                                     rule_id: "PFTUSW",
572:                                     message: format!(
573:                                         "The temporary variable {name} might be used after the PARFOR loop on line {line}."
574:                                     ),
575:                                     severity: Severity::Warning,
576:                                     byte_range: lhs_node.start_byte()..lhs_node.end_byte(),
577:                                     line: pos.row + 1,
578:                                     column: pos.column + 1,
579:                                     fix: None,
580:                                 });
581:                             }
582:                         }
583:                     }
584:                 }
585:             }
586: 
587:             // PFUIXW: index variable used after the loop.
588:             if self.is_check_enabled("PFUIXW") {
589:                 if let Some(ref idx) = idx_var {
590:                     let uses = uses_after_parfor(&sym, idx, parfor.end_byte(), tree, true);
591:                     if let Some(line) = uses.first() {
592:                         let idx_node = find_parfor_index_identifier(*parfor);
593:                         let target = idx_node.unwrap_or(*parfor);
594:                         let pos = target.start_position();
595:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
596:                             rule_id: "PFUIXW",
597:                             message: format!(
598:                                 "The index variable {idx} might be used after the PARFOR loop on line {line}."
599:                             ),
600:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
601:                             byte_range: target.start_byte()..target.end_byte(),
602:                             line: pos.row + 1,
603:                             column: pos.column + 1,
604:                             fix: None,
605:                         });
606:                     }
607:                 }
608:             }
609:         }
610: 
611:         diagnostics
612:     }

614:     /// Shared COMPNOP/COMPNOT logic: extract the `(call, literal, operator)`
615:     /// triple from a `comparison_operator` node when exactly one operand is a
616:     /// `function_call` and the other is the `true`/`false` literal.
617:     pub(crate) fn comparison_with_literal<'a>(
618:         &self,
619:         node: Node<'a>,
620:         source: &'a str,
621:     ) -> Option<(Node<'a>, Node<'a>, String)> {
622:         let lhs = node.child(0)?;
623:         let rhs = node.child(2)?;
624:         let op = find_operator_text(node, source);
625: 
626:         let (call_node, literal_node) = match (lhs.kind(), rhs.kind()) {
627:             ("function_call", "identifier") => (lhs, rhs),
628:             ("identifier", "function_call") => (rhs, lhs),
629:             _ => return None,
630:         };
631:         let literal = node_text(literal_node, source).trim();
632:         if literal == "true" || literal == "false" {
633:             Some((call_node, literal_node, op))
634:         } else {
635:             None
636:         }
637:     }
638: }

796: /// Check whether a node has a child of the given kind.
797: pub(crate) fn has_child_of_kind(node: Node, kind: &str) -> bool {
798:     let count = node.child_count();
799:     for i in 0..count {
800:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
801:             if child.kind() == kind {
802:                 return true;
803:             }
804:         }
805:     }
806:     false
807: }

811:     let count = node.child_count();
812:     for i in 0..count {
813:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
814:             if child.kind() == kind {
815:                 return Some(child);
816:             }
817:         }

885: /// Find the operator text in a binary/boolean/comparison operator node.
886: pub(crate) fn find_operator_text<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> String {
887:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
888:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
889:         if !child.is_named() {
890:             let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
891:             let trimmed = text.trim();
892:             if !trimmed.is_empty() && trimmed != "(" && trimmed != ")" && trimmed != "," {
893:                 return trimmed.to_string();
894:             }
895:         }
896:     }
897: 
898:     if let Some(op_node) = node.child_by_field_name("operator") {
899:         return node_text(op_node, source).trim().to_string();
900:     }
901: 
902:     let text = node_text(node, source);
903:     for op in &[
904:         "==", "~=", ">=", "<=", "&&", "||", ">", "<", "&", "|", "+", "-", "*", "/", "^",
905:     ] {
906:         if text.contains(op) {
907:             return (*op).to_string();
908:         }
909:     }
910: 
911:     String::new()
912: }

918:         let kind = child.kind();
919:         if kind == "string" || kind == "char_vector" {
920:             return true;

922:         // Also check for string literal wrapped in parens, etc.
923:         if child.is_named() && node_has_string_child(child) {
924:             return true;
925:         }
926:     }
927:     false
928: }

930: /// Classify the type of eval usage based on argument text patterns.
931: pub(crate) fn classify_eval_usage(
932:     args_text: &str,
933:     config: &GoodPracticesConfig,
934: ) -> (&'static str, &'static str) {
935:     // EVLDOT: dynamic field access patterns like `eval(['s.' fieldname])`
936:     if (args_text.contains("s.") || args_text.contains(".("))
937:         && config.disabled_checks.iter().all(|c| c != "EVLDOT")
938:     {
939:         return (
940:             "EVLDOT",
941:             "Avoid eval() for dynamic field access; use s.(fieldname) instead",
942:         );
943:     }
944: 
945:     // EVLSYS: system command patterns
946:     if (args_text.contains("system") || args_text.contains("dos") || args_text.contains("unix"))
947:         && config.disabled_checks.iter().all(|c| c != "EVLSYS")
948:     {
949:         return (
950:             "EVLSYS",
951:             "Avoid eval() for system commands; use system() directly",
952:         );
953:     }
954: 
955:     // EVLEQ: dynamic variable creation like `eval([varname ' = ...'])`
956:     if args_text.contains(" = ") && config.disabled_checks.iter().all(|c| c != "EVLEQ") {
957:         return (
958:             "EVLEQ",
959:             "Avoid eval() for dynamic variable creation; use containers.Map or struct fields",
960:         );
961:     }
962: 
963:     // EVLSEQVAR: sequential variable creation like `eval(['x' num2str(i)])`
964:     if (args_text.contains("num2str") || args_text.contains("int2str"))
965:         && config.disabled_checks.iter().all(|c| c != "EVLSEQVAR")
966:     {
967:         return (
968:             "EVLSEQVAR",
969:             "Avoid eval() to create sequential variables; use cell arrays or struct fields",
970:         );
971:     }
972: 
973:     // EVLCS: general eval usage (fallback)
974:     (
975:         "EVLCS",
976:         "Avoid eval(); it is slow, hard to debug, and a security risk",
977:     )
978: }

1003:                 }

1010: /// Count the depth of a field_expression chain (for CHAIN).
1011: pub(crate) fn field_chain_depth(node: Node) -> usize {
1012:     if node.kind() != "field_expression" {
1013:         return 0;
1014:     }
1015:     // The object child of a field_expression may itself be a field_expression.
1016:     let mut depth = 1;
1017:     if let Some(obj) = node.child_by_field_name("object").or_else(|| node.child(0)) {
1018:         depth += field_chain_depth(obj);
1019:     }
1020:     depth

1034:         current = p.parent();

7:             return Vec::new();
8:         }
9: 
10:         let func_name = match get_function_call_name(node, source) {
11:             Some(n) => n,

13:         };

15:         let (check_id, replacement) = match func_name {
16:             "prod" if self.is_check_enabled("LOGPROD") => ("LOGPROD", "all"),
17:             "min" if self.is_check_enabled("LOGMIN") => ("LOGMIN", "all"),
18:             "max" if self.is_check_enabled("LOGMAX") => ("LOGMAX", "any"),
19:             _ => return Vec::new(),
20:         };
21: 
22:         // Heuristic: check if the argument is likely logical (named with `is`, `has`,
23:         // or is a comparison result). We can't know types statically, so this is
24:         // limited to obvious patterns.
25:         let args_node = find_child_of_kind(node, "arguments");
26:         let first_arg = args_node.and_then(|a| first_named_child(a));
27:         let looks_logical = first_arg
28:             .map(|arg| {
29:                 let kind = arg.kind();
30:                 if kind == "comparison_operator" || kind == "boolean_operator" {
31:                     return true;
32:                 }
33:                 if kind == "identifier" {
34:                     let name = node_text(arg, source);
35:                     return name.starts_with("is")

4: 
5: # Language Specification
6: 
7: **Default severity:** Error
8: **Auto-fix:** No
9: **Category:** Language Specification
10: **Can be disabled:** Yes
11: 
12: ## What these checks do
13: 
14: These checks validate `arguments` blocks and their interaction with the function signature, matching MATLAB Code Analyzer's function validation checks (FV\* family plus the size checks `TINVALDIM` and `TTOOFEWDIMS`).
15: 
16: The checks operate on three groups:
17: 
18: - **Structure** — block attributes, repeating blocks, output blocks, and class-name name-value arguments.
19: - **Ordering** — argument declaration order, duplicates, and consistency with the function line.
20: - **Validation** — validation function rules and size constraints.
21: 
22: ## Check IDs
23: 
24: ### Structure
25: 
26: | Check ID | Message |
27: | -------- | ------- |
28: | `FVDREP` | Multiple Repeating arguments blocks are not supported. |
29: | `FVIOA` | Specifying both 'Input' and 'Output' attributes on the same arguments block is not supported. |
30: | `FVREPO` | Repeating input arguments block containing varargin must not have other arguments. |
31: | `FVVREP` | varargin can only be used inside repeating input arguments block. |
32: | `FVOVREP` | Output argument varargout can only be used inside a Repeating output arguments block. |
33: | `FVNREP` | Name-value arguments are not supported in a Repeating arguments block. |
34: | `FVREPD` | Default values are not supported in a Repeating arguments block. |
35: | `FVOOD` | Specifying a default value for an output argument is not supported. |
36: | `FVOOI` | Use of ignored arguments in output arguments block is not supported. |
37: | `FVOON` | Using name-value argument as output argument is not supported. |
38: | `FVORM` | Declaring multiple repeating output arguments is not supported. |
39: | `FVOBI` | Declare all input argument blocks before all output arguments blocks. |
40: | `FVATF` | Attribute values in arguments blocks must be logical constants. |
41: | `FVMCL` | Specifying multiple name-value structures using .? syntax and a class name is not supported. |
42: | `FVNDE` | When specifying name-value arguments using a class name, it is illegal to specify default values for the arguments. |
43: | `FVNVL` | When specifying name-value arguments using a class name, it is illegal to specify validation for the arguments. |
44: 
45: ### Ordering and consistency
46: 
47: | Check ID | Message |
48: | -------- | ------- |
49: | `FVORDI` | Ignored input arguments are not allowed after a Repeating arguments block or name-value arguments. |
50: | `FVORDN` | Positional arguments must be defined before name-value arguments. |
51: | `FVORDP` | Positional arguments must be defined in the following order: required, optional, and repeating. |
52: | `FVORDO` | Repeating output arguments must be defined after required output arguments. |
53: | `FVAPN` | Move name-value arguments that use the name=value syntax to the end of the argument list. |
54: | `FVDAN` | Using the same name as both a name-value argument structure and as a positional argument is not supported. |
55: | `FVDAP` | Positional argument can only be declared once. |
56: | `FVDNF` | Name-value argument can only be declared once. |
57: | `FVSOR` | Input arguments block declarations and the function line must contain the same input arguments in the same order, including ignored arguments. |
58: | `FVSORO` | Output arguments block declarations and the function line must contain the same output arguments in the same order. |
59: | `FVNIV` | This variable is not an input to the function and cannot be used in an arguments block. |
60: | `FVIDV` | Specifying validation or default value for ignored arguments is not supported. |
61: 
62: ### Validation functions and size
63: 
64: | Check ID | Message |
65: | -------- | ------- |
66: | `FVVIN` | Validation function must use the argument as an input. |
67: | `FVVCON` | For input arguments, validation functions must only use previously declared positional arguments, the argument being validated, or literals. |
68: | `FVOCON` | For output arguments, validation functions must only use the argument being validated or literals. |
69: | `FVUBD` | Argument is referenced before it is declared in the arguments block. |
70: | `FVOND` | Use of name-value arguments in default values is not supported. |
71: | `FVONV` | Use of name-value arguments without dotted name in the validation is not supported. |
72: | `FVBTN` | Use of this function is not supported in arguments blocks. |
73: | `FVNSC` | Use of nested functions is not supported in arguments blocks. |
74: | `TINVALDIM` | Each dimension must be a nonnegative integer number or a colon. |
75: | `TTOOFEWDIMS` | Specify at least two dimensions for size. |
76: 
77: ## Why these checks matter
78: 
79: - **Arguments blocks** are the primary mechanism for input/output validation in modern MATLAB; malformed blocks cause runtime errors at the call site.
80: - **Declaration order** rules exist because MATLAB resolves positional, optional, repeating, and name-value arguments left-to-right; violations are rejected by the interpreter.
81: - **Validation function restrictions** (using only the argument, previously declared positionals, and literals) keep validation deterministic and side-effect free.
82: - **Size constraint checks** catch dimension declarations that can never match a concrete array.
83: 
84: ## Examples
85: 
86: ### Correct
87: 
88: ```matlab
89: function y = f(a, b, opts)
90:     arguments
91:         a (1,1) double
92:         b = 3
93:         opts.Name {mustBeReal}
94:     end
95:     y = a + b;
96: end
97: 
98: function [out, varargout] = g(x)
99:     arguments
100:         x (1,:) double {mustBeReal}
101:     end
102:     arguments (Output)
103:         out (1,1) double
104:     end
105:     arguments (Repeating)
106:         varargout
107:     end
108: end
109: ```
110: 
111: ### Incorrect
112: 
113: ```matlab
114: function y = f(a, b)
115:     arguments
116:         b = 3                 % FVORDP: optional before required
117:         a (1,1) double
118:         opts.Name = 'x'       % FVORDN: name-value after positional (also FVAPN)
119:     end
120:     y = a;
121: end
122: 
123: function [y] = g(x)
124:     arguments (Output)
125:         y (1,1) double = 5    % FVOOD: default value for an output
126:     end
127:     arguments (Input)
128:         x (1,1) double        % FVOBI: input block after output block
129:     end
130: end
131: ```
132: 
133: ## Configuration
134: 
135: These checks are part of the `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` rule. Disable individual checks via `disabled_checks`:
136: 
137: ```toml title=".mlt.toml"
138: [lint.rules.LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE]
139: disabled_checks = ["FVNIV", "TTOOFEWDIMS"]
140: ```
141: 
142: ### Parameters
143: 
144: | Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
145: | --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
146: | `disabled_checks` | array of strings | `[]` | Check IDs to disable within the language spec engine |
147: 
148: ## Automatic fixes
149: 
150: No automatic fixes are available for these checks.
151: 
152: ## Target node types
153: 
154: These checks run at the file level and inspect `function_definition` nodes and their `arguments_statement` children:
155: 
156: - `function_definition` — matched to extracted function metadata by byte range
157: - `arguments_statement` — an `arguments ... end` block, grouped with its attributes and arguments
158: - `attributes` — the block's `(Input)`, `(Output)`, `(Repeating)` attributes
159: - `property` — a single argument declaration
160: - `property_name` — a name-value argument declaration (`struct.field`)
161: - `class_property` — a `.?ClassName` name-value declaration
162: - `dimensions` — the size constraint
163: - `validation_functions` — the `{...}` validation function list
164: - `default_value` — the `= value` default expression
165: 
166: ## Related rules
167: 
168: - `FVNST` — Arguments blocks in nested functions
169: - `VTPOD` — Argument validation order (size, then class, then functions)
170: - `FVINR` — Add Input attribute to the input arguments block (readability)
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: # Language Specification - Parfor Variable, Slicing, and Reduction Checks
175: 
176: These checks are also part of the `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` rule. They validate parfor loop headers, banned functions, sliced output variables, and temporary/reduction variable classification, matching MATLAB Code Analyzer's parfor checks (PF\* family plus FPFORP and FWFORP).
177: 
178: ## Check IDs
179: 
180: ### Banned functions in parfor
181: 
182: | Check ID | Message |
183: | -------- | ------- |
184: | `PFEVC` | EVALIN('caller') and ASSIGNIN('caller') are invalid inside a PARFOR loop. |
185: | `PFINPT` | 'inputname' is not supported in parfor loops. |
186: | `PFNACK` | 'narginchk' and 'nargoutchk' cannot be used in parfor loops. |
187: | `PFNAIO` | 'nargin' and 'nargout' require a function argument in parfor loops. |
188: | `PFLD` | 'load' must assign to an output variable in parfor loops. |
189: | `PFSV` | SAVE cannot be called in a PARFOR loop without the '-fromstruct' option. |
190: | `FPFORP` | 'fprintf' is writing to a file opened with read permission only. |
191: | `FWFORP` | 'fwrite' is writing to a file opened with read permission only. |
192: | `PFCEL` | The function does not support cell arrays (argument N). |
193: 
194: ### Parfor loop variable restrictions
195: 
196: | Check ID | Message |
197: | -------- | ------- |
198: | `PFANSLP` | 'ans' is not supported as a parfor loop variable. |
199: | `PFANSNS` | 'ans' is not supported as a for loop variable in parfor loops. |
200: | `PFVSUB` | Indexing parfor loop variables is not supported in parfor loops. |
201: | `PFFSUB` | Indexing a nested for loop variable is not supported in parfor loops. |
202: | `PFMLTI` | The nested for loop variable must not be assigned other than by its for statement. |
203: | `PFRNG` | The range of a PARFOR statement must be increasing consecutive integers. |
204: 
205: ### Sliced variable rules
206: 
207: | Check ID | Message |
208: | -------- | ------- |
209: | `PFSLO` | Variable is indexed using the parfor loop variable, but it is not a valid sliced output variable. |
210: | `PFSLRD` | Invalid combination of sliced indexing and non-indexed reads of a sliced output variable. |
211: | `PFSLW` | Multiple sliced accesses must all use the same list of subscripts. |
212: | `PFANON` | Using a sliced output variable in an anonymous function is not supported in parfor loops. |
213: | `PFCTXT` | When indexing a sliced variable with a nested for loop variable, the sliced variable must be inside the for loop that defines its range. |
214: | `PFFRNG` | When indexing a sliced variable with a nested for loop variable, the range must be a row vector of positive constant numbers. |
215: 
216: ### Temporary and reduction variables
217: 
218: | Check ID | Message |
219: | -------- | ------- |
220: | `PFUTMP` | Temporary variable must be set inside the parfor loop before it is used. |
221: | `PFUTVR` | Variable may have been intended as a reduction variable, but is an uninitialized temporary. |
222: | `PFINCR` | Using different reduction functions with the same reduction variable is not supported in parfor loops. |
223: | `PFNAR` | Subtracting reduction variable from expressions is not supported in parfor loops. |
224: | `PFRFH` | The PARFOR reduction function must be a function name or a broadcast variable. |
225: | `PFUNK` | The PARFOR loop cannot run due to the way a variable is used. |
226: | `PFVARS` | Parfor loop contains too many variables. |
227: 
228: ## Why these checks matter
229: 
230: - **Parfor transparency** requires that every iteration be independent; functions that inspect the caller workspace (`evalin`/`assignin` with `'caller'`, `inputname`, `nargin`/`nargout`) or mutate the base workspace (`load`, `save`) break this model.
231: - **Sliced output variables** must be indexed by the parfor loop variable with a consistent subscript list; violations either serialize the loop, produce race conditions, or are rejected by the parallel pool.
232: - **Temporary variables** must be assigned before first use in every iteration; uninitialized temporaries are a common source of nondeterministic results.
233: - **Reduction variables** support a fixed set of associative/commutative functions; mixing operators or subtracting the reduction variable from an expression is rejected.
234: 
235: ## Examples
236: 
237: ### Correct
238: 
239: ```matlab
240: parfor i = 1:10
241:     x(i) = i;              % sliced output with consistent subscripts
242: end
243: 
244: s = 0;
245: parfor i = 1:10
246:     s = s + x(i);          % valid reduction (initialized before the loop)
247: end
248: ```
249: 
250: ### Incorrect
251: 
252: ```matlab
253: parfor i = 1:10
254:     evalin('caller', 'x'); % PFEVC
255:     load('data.mat');      % PFLD
256:     t = i * 2;
257:     y = t(i);              % PFSLO: t is a temporary, not a sliced output
258:     s = x(i) - s;          % PFNAR: subtracting reduction variable s
259: end
260: ```
261: 
262: ## Configuration
263: 
264: These checks are part of the `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` rule. Disable individual checks via `disabled_checks`:
265: 
266: ```toml title=".mlt.toml"
267: [lint.rules.LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE]
268: disabled_checks = ["PFEVC", "PFSLO"]
269: ```
270: 
271: ### Parameters
272: 
273: | Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
274: | --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
275: | `disabled_checks` | array of strings | `[]` | Check IDs to disable within the language spec engine |
276: 
277: ## Automatic fixes
278: 
279: No automatic fixes are available for these checks.
280: 
281: ## Target node types
282: 
283: These checks run at the file level and inspect the following tree-sitter nodes inside parfor bodies:
284: 
285: - `for_statement` — a `parfor` or nested `for` loop (distinguished by the `parfor`/`for` keyword child)
286: - `function_call` — banned functions, sliced/indexed accesses, and loop-variable indexing
287: - `assignment` — temporary, sliced, and reduction variable classification
288: - `command` — command-syntax `load`, `save`, `nargin`, `nargout`
289: - `identifier` — whole (non-indexed) reads
290: - `lambda` — anonymous functions referencing sliced output variables
291: 
292: ## Related rules
293: 
294: - `PFPF` — Nested parfor inside parfor
295: - `PFFORA` — Assignment to a for-loop variable inside parfor
296: - `PFXST` — Assignment to the parfor loop variable
297: - `PFUIXE` — Parfor index used in eval (bugs engine)
298: - `PFRNC` — Reduction not consistent in parfor (bugs engine)
299: 
300: ---
301: 
302: # Language Specification - Class/Method Attribute, Constructor, and Superclass Checks
303: 
304: These checks are also part of the `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` rule. They validate class and member attribute combinations, Constant and WeakHandle property usage, constructor/superclass call patterns, and method signature limits, matching MATLAB Code Analyzer's class checks (MC\* family plus `MTAGS3`, `MTMAT`, `MWKCL`, `MWKCT`, `MWKREF`).
305: 
306: ## Check IDs
307: 
308: ### Class attribute conflicts
309: 
310: | Check ID | Message |
311: | -------- | ------- |
312: | `MABSEAC` | Instance properties and methods are illegal in classes that are both Sealed and Abstract. |
313: | `MCSWA` | A sealed class cannot specify allowed subclasses. |
314: | `MTMAT` | Attribute can only be set once. |
315: | `MTAGS3` | Cannot use the Access attribute when using the SetAccess or GetAccess attribute. |
316: 
317: ### Abstract/Sealed members
318: 
319: | Check ID | Message |
320: | -------- | ------- |
321: | `MABSEAM` | A method cannot be both Abstract and Sealed. |
322: | `MCMSP` | Private method cannot be Abstract. |
323: | `MCAPP` | Private property cannot be Abstract. |
324: | `MCGSA` | Method tries to set or get an abstract property. |
325: | `MCPSG` | Set or get method must be fully defined in the class definition file. |
326: 
327: ### Constant and WeakHandle properties
328: 
329: | Check ID | Message |
330: | -------- | ------- |
331: | `MCCSOP` | Unable to modify Constant property. |
332: | `MCSCN` | Method tries to set a constant property. |
333: | `MWKCL` | A WeakHandle property must restrict its type using a class validation. |
334: | `MWKCT` | Specifying both WeakHandle and Constant attributes on the same property is not supported. |
335: | `MWKREF` | Specifying both WeakHandle and Dependent attributes is invalid. |
336: 
337: ### Constructor/superclass calls
338: 
339: | Check ID | Message |
340: | -------- | ------- |
341: | `MCCBS` | A superclass constructor is being called, but the name is not a declared superclass name. |
342: | `MCCBU` | This superclass constructor is called after a use of the constructed object. |
343: | `MCCMC` | Constructor for superclass can only be called once. |
344: | `MCSCC` | To call the superclass constructor, the subclass constructor name must match the subclass name. |
345: | `MCSCF` | A superclass constructor must be assigned to the first constructor output argument. |
346: | `MCSCO` | A superclass constructor must be called using the first constructor output argument. |
347: | `MCSCT` | Superclass constructor call must not be conditionalized or be part of another expression. |
348: | `MCSMO` | Returning multiple outputs from a superclass object initialization is not supported. |
349: | `MCSCM` | To call a superclass method, the method name must match the subclass method name. |
350: 
351: ### Method signatures
352: 
353: | Check ID | Message |
354: | -------- | ------- |
355: | `MCMIO` | Method has too many inputs or outputs. |
356: | `MCMTP` | TestParameterDefinition methods must be Static. |
357: | `MCPIN` | Unable to initialize class property to an instance of the class itself. |
358: 
359: ## Why these checks matter
360: 
361: - **Mutually exclusive attributes** (`Sealed`+`Abstract`, `WeakHandle`+`Constant`, `WeakHandle`+`Dependent`, `Access`+`SetAccess`) describe states MATLAB cannot represent; the class is rejected at definition time.
362: - **Abstract members** must not be private or sealed, and set/get methods must be fully implemented — abstract accessors leave the property unusable.
363: - **Constant properties** cannot be reassigned after class load; assignments in the constructor or other methods are silently lost or error at runtime.
364: - **Superclass constructor calls** (`obj@SuperClass(...)`) must be the first operation, unconditional, assigned to the first output, and reference a declared superclass — violations produce undefined objects or runtime errors.
365: - **WeakHandle properties** need a class validation so MATLAB knows the concrete type the handle refers to.
366: 
367: ## Examples
368: 
369: ### Correct
370: 
371: ```matlab
372: classdef GoodClass < Base
373:     properties (Constant)
374:         K = 42
375:     end
376:     properties (WeakHandle)
377:         ref SomeHandleClass
378:     end
379:     methods
380:         function obj = GoodClass()
381:             obj = obj@Base();
382:         end
383:     end
384: end
385: ```
386: 
387: ### Incorrect
388: 
389: ```matlab
390: classdef (Sealed, Abstract) BadClass
391:     properties
392:         x                          % MABSEAC: instance property in Sealed+Abstract class
393:     end
394:     properties (WeakHandle, Constant)
395:         w                          % MWKCT
396:     end
397:     methods (Abstract, Sealed)
398:         function y = f(obj)        % MABSEAM
399:         end
400:     end
401:     methods
402:         function obj = BadClass()
403:             obj.y = 1;             % MCCBU: object used before superclass constructor
404:             if true
405:                 obj = obj@Base();  % MCSCT: conditionalized superclass constructor
406:             end
407:             [obj, z] = obj@Base(); % MCCMC + MCSMO: second call with multiple outputs
408:         end
409:     end
410: end
411: ```
412: 
413: ## Configuration
414: 
415: These checks are part of the `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` rule. Disable individual checks via `disabled_checks`:
416: 
417: ```toml title=".mlt.toml"
418: [lint.rules.LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE]
419: disabled_checks = ["MABSEAC", "MCSWA"]
420: ```
421: 
422: ### Parameters
423: 
424: | Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
425: | --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
426: | `disabled_checks` | array of strings | `[]` | Check IDs to disable within the language spec engine |
427: 
428: ## Automatic fixes
429: 
430: No automatic fixes are available for these checks.
431: 
432: ## Target node types
433: 
434: These checks run at the file level and use both `FileMeta`/`ClassMeta` metadata and raw tree walks:
435: 
436: - `class_definition` — class-level attribute checks (MABSEAC, MCSWA, MTMAT, MTAGS3)
437: - `properties` — property attribute checks (MCAPP, MCGSA, MWKCL, MWKCT, MWKREF, MCPIN)
438: - `methods` — method attribute checks (MABSEAM, MCMSP, MCPSG, MCMTP, MCMIO)
439: - `function_definition` — constructor/superclass call checks (MCCBS, MCCBU, MCCMC, MCSCF, MCSCN, MCSCO, MCSCT, MCSMO, MCSCC, MCSCM, MCCSOP)
440: - `assignment` — `obj.Prop = value` assignments to Constant properties
441: 
442: ## Related rules
443: 
444: - `MCFIL`, `MCDIR`, `MCRED`, `MCCBD` — class file/name structure checks
445: - `MCS2I`, `MCS1O`, `MCG1I`, `MCG1O`, `MCSGP` — set/get method signature checks
446: - `CTOINE`, `CTORO`, `MHERIT` — constructor construction checks in this engine

7: **Default severity:** Warning

12: ## What these checks do
13: 
14: These checks cover function-call conventions: `sprintf`/`fprintf` format strings that do not agree with the argument count, `for` loop iterator variables that are reassigned inside the loop, `import` statements that do not run first in a function, dynamic-code functions (`eval`, `evalc`, `evalin`, `feval`) used as sub-expressions, `onCleanup` outputs that are discarded or assigned to `~`, and the platform-specific `computer('arch')` query.
15: 
16: ## Check IDs
17: 
18: | Check ID | Message |
19: | -------- | ------- |
20: | `CTPCT` | The format might not agree with the argument count. |
21: | `FXSET` | Loop index `VAR_NAME` is changed inside of a FOR loop. |
22: | `SIMPT` | This import statement runs before any other code in function `VAR_NAME`. Consider placing it at the top of the function body. |
23: | `TLEV` | `VAR_NAME` could be very inefficient unless it is a top-level statement in its function. |
24: | `UNONC` | Assign the onCleanup output argument to a variable. Do not use the tilde operator (~) in place of a variable. |
25: | `MIPC1` | Calling the computer function with 'arch' returns 'win64', 'glnxa64', or 'maci64'. |
26: | `ATTF` | The Code Analyzer is unable to determine if the expression assigned to the `Abstract` attribute evaluates to true or false. |
27: | `ATTOF` | Setting the class attribute `Abstract` to false is not recommended. |
28: | `MCPO` | `SetObservable`/`GetObservable`/`AbortSet` property has no effect in a value class. |
29: | `MCSAC` | `SetAccess` cannot be set on Constant properties. |
30: | `MOBSRV` | `SetObservable`/`GetObservable` on a Constant property has no effect. |
31: | `MDEPIN` | Default values should not be assigned to dependent properties. |
32: | `MCCPI` | Initialize the Constant property or make it an Abstract Constant property. |
33: | `MGMD` | `get` method should be implemented for each dependent property without private `GetAccess`. |
34: | `MCCPE` | Attempting to call a property or event as a function. |
35: | `MTHANS` | Using `ANS` as a method name is not recommended. |
36: | `MHERM` | Parenthesize the multiplication of a variable and its transpose. |
37: | `MNUML` | To create a square matrix, use `VAR_NAME(numel(...), numel(...))`. |
38: | `COMFS` | This comma makes the file a script. Therefore, all functions in the file are local functions. |
39: | `DUALC` | Command might be prematurely ended by comma. |
40: | `RMFLD` | RMFIELD output must be assigned back to the structure. |

45: | `SUBSINDEX` | Do not overload 'subsindex' for fundamental data types. |
